meta.mission: USAAF Eighth Air Force Mission 115, Schweinfurt, 14 October 1943
meta.coordinate_system: metres; x = right (starboard of formation lead), y = up, z = back (behind lead). Offsets are relative to the parent formation's lead aircraft.
meta.confidence_scale: VERIFIED = mission-specific primary record or several agreeing credible sources; PROBABLE = single credible source or doctrine of the period; ESTIMATE = derived/assumed for the game, no direct source; UNKNOWN = searched, not found.

aircraft_reference.note: B-17F span 103 ft 9 in, length 74 ft 9 in (standard published figures), used only to derive clearances.

aircraft_per_element.note: Three-ship Vee (lead, left wing, right wing). 303rd assembly chart shows three-ship rows.

left_wing.note: Derived from training-manual minimums: 50 ft wingtip clearance (span 31.6 m + 15.2 m = 47 m lateral) and 50 ft nose-to-tail (length 22.8 m + 15.2 m = 38 m back). Combat crews often flew tighter. Vertical offset not documented: 0 by default.

wingman_vertical_step.note: No 1943 combat figure found for wingman step-up/down within an element. Configurable; 0-15 m reasonable.

aircraft_per_squadron.note: Two elements (6) plus, in the 21-plane box, a seventh 'tail-end' aircraft. 303rd on 14 Oct: lead squadron 6, the other two 7 each (3-3-1 rows).

second_element_lead.note: 303rd chart shows second element directly behind the first. Training manual: >=50 ft (15 m) vertical between elements and >=50 ft horizontal clearance from first-element wingmen (z = 38 + 22.8 + 15 = 76 m). Early-1943 squadrons ~150 ft (46 m) top-to-bottom (S18), so -30 m used.

seventh_aircraft.note: 303rd chart places the 7th aircraft centred behind the second element. Offsets assumed.

aircraft_per_group_documented.note: Dispatch sizes on 14 Oct ranged 11 (91st) to 20 (303rd); after aborts groups over the target were often 10-18. The 36-plane group box introduced in Oct 1943 (S18) was NOT used this day.

nominal_group_size.note: 18-21 plane box doctrine (summer 1943); 21-plane box standard Jan-Sept 1943 (Bowman via S18).

high_squadron.note: Vertical +100 ft (30 m) from Craven & Cate summer-1943 diagram (lead 25,000 / high 25,100 ft) - PROBABLE. Training manual instead gives 150 ft above, 100 ft behind (S17). Lateral side and distances are estimates read from the plan-view diagram (high and low squadrons trail on opposite sides); side varied with sun/stacking.

low_squadron.note: Vertical -250 ft (76 m) from Craven & Cate diagram (24,750 ft) - PROBABLE. Lateral/longitudinal estimates.

group_box_total_depth.note: 750 ft top-to-bottom aircraft in summer-1943 combat box diagram.

groups_per_wing.note: Lead, high, low. On 14 Oct the 40th CW effectively flew with two groups after the 305th joined the 1st CW (S7, S15).

high_group.note: Vertical +1,000 ft (305 m): documented for this mission (351st briefing: lead 91st 23,000 ft, high 351st 24,000 ft) and in the doctrine diagram. Lateral and trail estimated to fit Freeman's wing box (~2,000 ft / 610 m across, ~7,000 ft / 2,130 m deep, S18).

low_group.note: Vertical -1,000 ft from doctrine diagram (lead box 25,000, low box 24,000). Low group altitude for 14 Oct not stated in S2 (implied ~22,000 ft). x, z estimates.

wing_box_envelope.note: Freeman (Mighty Eighth War Manual) via Wikipedia: ~3,000 x 7,000 x 2,000 ft. Craven & Cate diagram: 3,000 ft overall vertical. S19 (unsourced) gives 1.3 mi wide x 0.3 mi deep for a Feb-1943 wedge - disagreement on depth.

first_division_wing_order.note: 351st briefing: '1st C.W. - Second, 40th CBW Lead, 41st CBW Third'. As flown: 305th joined the 1st CW, the 40th (92nd+306th) 'tagged along with the 41st' (S7) and the 351st leader credited the 1st CW leader with leading the Air Division (S2). Craven & Cate still call the 40th the leading wing. Offer an 'as_flown' variant: ['1st (+305th)', '41st', '40th (92nd, 306th)'] - PROBABLE at best.

third_division_wing_order.note: Only the lead is supported (96th/45th CBW led the 3rd Division: S22 [citation needed], S16, S23). Order of the 4th and 13th behind it NOT FOUND; one search excerpt (source not identified) instead had the 13th CW forming first with the 4th and 45th trailing. Treat as configurable.

interval_between_wings.note: No planned figure found. Derived: 1st AD bombed 1439-1445 (S9) with the second wing's 351st at 1441 (S2), i.e. roughly 2-3 min between wings over the target. At 222 mph TAS (99 m/s) 2 min = ~11.9 km. Range 1-3 min.

interval_between_groups_on_bomb_run.note: On the bomb run groups went into trail: the 351st 'took the normal trail behind the 91st and 381st Groups' (S2), turning on the IP at 1438 and bombing at 1441. Interval not stated; ~1 min assumed.

groups_into_trail_from_IP.note: Group-level bombing ('Method of Attack - Group'); leader sighted range and deflection, deputy range; others dropped on leader.

lateral_separation_penetration.note: 'cross enemy defenses abreast, some 30 miles apart' (Craven & Cate); map shows 3rd Division track south of the 1st. Treat as plan; actual separation varied.

time_separation_briefed.note: '3rd ATF same target 30 minutes behind us'. Conflicts with Craven & Cate 'abreast'.

time_separation_at_target_actual.note: Bombing 1439-1445 (1st) vs 1451-1457 (3rd) (S9); corroborated by 351st 1441 and 100th 1454. 1st AD itself was ~13 min late (S2).

third_division_route_dogleg.value: after escort left near Eupen: south toward Trier/Mosel, then east to the IP, converging on Schweinfurt
third_division_route_dogleg.note: Dog-leg visible on Craven & Cate map (S5); waypoint names only from low-reliability S16.

english_coast_out.note: Times from individual group records; do not imply the 3rd crossed earlier overall.

briefed_altitude.note: 24,000 ft ('Altitude and time on Oxygen: 24,000 - 5 1/2 hours').

bombing_altitude_true.note: 351st 23,550 ft true above target; 303rd 24,050 ft. 100th reset bombsight 1,000 ft lower on the run (S8).

post_target_altitude.note: 'Descend after target to 21,000''; enemy coast out at Ault 16:43 at 21,000 ft.

bomb_run_ias.note: Calculated indicated airspeed 150 mph at release (351st lead).

cruise_ias.note: No en-route figure found; use 150 mph IAS. Wind at altitude 220 deg / 30 mph (S2).

ip.value: Wurzburg (1st Division, 351st record); 3rd Division IP described as near Darmstadt (S16, low reliability)

axis_of_attack_true.note: True heading 64, drift, true track 61 at release.

straight_and_level_before_release.note: Flak report 40 s; bombing flight record 60 s. 5-degree S-turns on the run-in before that.

rally.value: right turn to 130 deg true after release, descend to 21,000 ft

value: Base/assembly over East Anglia (1st CW rendezvous Cambridge)
waypoints.confidence: VERIFIED (351st flak report and briefing; partly illegible in source)
waypoints.note: Some intermediate names unreadable in the transcription.

penetration_p47.value: 1 P-47 group (~50) per task force from 51°30'N 04°15'E to limit of range; 56th and 353rd FG made contact; 4th FG failed to find bombers
penetration_p47.note: Turn-back near Aachen, ~240 mi from British coast (S3), ~13:30-13:33 (S2, S24).

withdrawal.value: 1 P-47 group per force planned from ~60 mi inland to mid-Channel, 4 sqn Spitfire IX to mid-Channel, 2 sqn Spitfire IX straggler sweep; largely prevented by weather
withdrawal.note: 351st navigator: 'We had no fighter escort home'.

p38_sweep.value: planned P-38 group sweep of Flushing area; not operational until next day
